thread.title: The subtle sign of promise for stocks, from a Wall Street veteran - MarketWatch

author: Victor Reklaitis
title: The subtle sign of promise for stocks, from a Wall Street veteran - MarketWatch
text:
The Dow just might saunter to a weekly win, as joy over Memorial Day weekend apparently overcomes any jitters over North Korea or Europe’s latest regulatory maneuver.
Count JonesTrading’s Michael O’Rourke among the strategists marveling at the stock market’s resilience.
“From a technical perspective, the market has been subtly impressive through these first 100 days,” he says, while sharing the graphic below that’s our chart of the day .
Here’s how 2018 stacks up after 100 trading days. Ahead of the 101st trading day of 2018, O’Rourke notes the S&P 500 has closed in the green 57% of the time so far this year, on par with 2017’s full-year reading.
“The key difference was 2017 finished the year up 22%,” he adds, while the S&P is only up 2% so far this year.
But the veteran strategist sounds mostly full of admiration at the moment. Rising interest rates haven’t derailed U.S. stocks, and equities have dealt with the earnings season’s “as good as it gets” theme, says O’Rourke, who has offered bearish takes from time to time .
“The geopolitical headlines have essentially been one negative story after another,” he also writes in his latest “Closing Print” note to clients. “Overall, the equity market has absorbed the headwinds in stride.”
Key market gauges Futures for the Dow YMM8, -0.30% , S&P 500 ESM8, -0.33% and Nasdaq-100 NQM8, +0.11% are trading lower. The Dow DJIA, -0.23% , S&P SPX, -0.25% and Nasdaq Composite COMP, +0.13% are on track for weekly gains that range from 0.4% to 1%, as of yesterday’s close .
Europe SXXP, +0.14% is mostly rising, after Asia finished mixed . Oil CLN8, -4.33% is slumping as key producers consider increasing their output, while gold GCM8, -0.20% and the dollar index DXY, +0.43% are gaining. Bitcoin BTCUSD, -2.25% is changing hands around $7,500.
See the Market Snapshot column for the latest action. And we’ve got you covered on which markets are closed on Memorial Day .
The Quote: Getty Images North Korea’s Kim Kye Gwan to Trump: Call me maybe? “We express our willingness to sit down face-to-face with the U.S. and resolve issues anytime and in any format.” — Kim Kye Gwan, a senior official in North Korea’s foreign ministry, adopts a conciliatory tone after President Trump nixed a much-anticipated summit with Kim Jong Un.
The call Ad-tech companies look like losers as the European Union’s new General Data Protection Regulation takes effect today, according to a Digiday report .
“So far, two U.S. ad-tech vendors, Verve and Drawbridge, have exited Europe and cited GDPR as a core reason,” the report says. “There will be others who decide that risking the burden of costs in getting compliant, along with the difficulty of gaining user consent for multiple data purposes, is simply not worth it.”
Read more: Your online privacy is about to get a lot more secure
And see: 5 things to know about the GDPR rules taking effect Friday
GDPR will speed up consolidation in the fragmented ad-tech industry, says an Economist report that also views the sector as a loser due to the EU’s new data-handling rules.
Other pundits say Facebook FB, -0.51% and Google GOOG, -0.26% GOOGL, -0.06% will be GDPR winners , but there are some who aren’t giving them any medals yet. Other publicly traded players in this industry are Marin Software MRIN, -0.91% , Criteo CRTO, +0.12% and Rakuten 4755, -1.59% , according to a Woodside Capital report .
And the Chicago Tribune (owned by Tronc TRNC, +1.43% ), Instapaper, the LA Times (which Tronc has sold), and Lee’s LEE, +2.04% St. Louis Post-Dispatch are among the companies whose websites went dark in most European countries this morning — a sign they’d rather lose the income than risk a hefty EU fine.
